source: Ye, Zhao, Leake, Wang, Crandall (2021) Applying the Case Difference Heuristic to Learn Adaptations from Deep Network Features
finding: Learned adaptation (case difference heuristic on CNN features) improves the retrieved solution in most settings, but not all. A plain regressor beats the CBR system when the query is familiar.
numbers: Age prediction from face images. Normal setting, L1 retrieval: error 9.58 before adaptation, 8.14 after. Siamese retrieval: 7.49 before, 7.86 after (adaptation made it worse). Constant baseline 12.94. Baseline regressor was best in the normal setting.
limits: One domain (face age regression), one lab group. The results table was garbled in text extraction; only values read cleanly are quoted.
agent_relevance: Editing is not free. An edit step can lower quality when retrieval is already good. Our S5 should compare the edited and unedited candidate and keep the better one.

source: Ye, Zhao, Leake, Wang, Crandall (2021) Applying the Case Difference Heuristic to Learn Adaptations from Deep Network Features
finding: Adaptation helps most when the query is far from the stored cases (novel queries). The benefit grows with distance.
numbers: Novel-query setting (train on ages 20-50, test on <20, 50-70, >70): Siamese+adaptation was the best system overall. For the >70 group, Siamese error 33.05 fell to 28.83 after adaptation; L1 35.84 fell to 32.11. Adaptation improved the initial solution in every novel-query cell.
limits: Regression with numeric solutions. Not text or code.
agent_relevance: Edit-a-retrieved-solution earns its cost on out-of-distribution problems. For problems very like a stored case, plain reuse may be as good. Route by distance (O7).

source: Ye, Zhao, Leake, Wang, Crandall (2021) Applying the Case Difference Heuristic to Learn Adaptations from Deep Network Features
finding: Retrieval and adaptation trained separately drift out of sync. Retrieval picks the nearest case, but the adapter was trained on random far pairs, so near cases get a poor edit.
numbers: Only one cell of the 2x2 got worse after adaptation: Siamese+adaptation, normal setting (7.49 to 7.86). Authors point to adaptation-guided retrieval and Leake and Ye 2021 alternating optimisation as fixes.
limits: The explanation is the authors' reading. No ablation isolates the cause.
agent_relevance: Pick cases for how editable they are, not only how similar. Matches our retrieval-by-value idea.

source: d'Aquin, Badra, Lafrogne, Lieber, Napoli, Szathmary (2006) Adaptation Knowledge Discovery from a Case Base (CABAMAKA)
finding: Classic adaptation knowledge acquisition: mine pairs of cases for rules that map problem differences to solution differences, with an expert filtering the rules.
numbers: Breast cancer treatment CBR system; reported as 'successfully tested', but no accuracy figures in this short paper.
limits: No quantitative evaluation. Weak evidence of effect; it shows the method, not its payoff.
agent_relevance: Adaptation rules can be mined from the memory itself. For us: store pairs (difference in problem, difference in solution) as reusable edit operators.

source: Badra, Lieber, d'Aquin, et al. (2007) Case Base Mining for Adaptation Knowledge Acquisition
finding: Formal concept analysis over all ordered pairs of source cases yields candidate adaptation rules; an analyst interprets them.
numbers: n=647 cases, support threshold 10%: 2,344 frequent closed itemsets in about 2 minutes on a PC. Only those with changes on both the problem side and the solution side are kept as rule candidates.
quote: More substantial experiments have to be carried out for an effective evaluation.
limits: Authors state that more substantial experiments are needed for an effective evaluation. Domain-bound (classes of oncology patients).
agent_relevance: Mining yields many candidate rules and a human must prune them. Rule quality control is the bottleneck, not rule generation.

source: Badra, Cordier, Lieber (2009) Opportunistic Adaptation Knowledge Discovery
finding: Trigger adaptation-knowledge learning at problem-solving time, only when adaptation fails, to cut expert effort.
numbers: Method paper. Calls adaptation 'the Achilles' heel' of case-based reasoning because the needed knowledge is domain specific and hard to acquire.
limits: No headline numbers read. Method and discussion only.
agent_relevance: Learn the edit rule when an edit fails, not in bulk beforehand. Fits a post-failure LOOK BACK step.

source: Leake, Smyth, Keane et al. adaptation-guided retrieval (Deja Vu experiments, 1994-1998)
finding: Search-result summary only: adaptation-guided retrieval is reported to beat standard similarity retrieval on accuracy and efficiency in case-based design experiments.
numbers: No numbers read. Seen only as a search snippet this session; the page itself returned 403.
limits: Not opened. Unverified; do not cite figures.
agent_relevance: Strong prior that retrieval should rank by ease of adaptation. Needs a primary-source read before we rely on it.

source: Jalali and Leake: ensemble adaptation-guided retrieval (EAGR)
finding: Search snippet only: an ensemble of adaptation rules is used to favour cases whose solutions the rules can adapt, tested against k-NN on numeric prediction.
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Not opened. Unverified. Year approximate.
agent_relevance: Same as above: pick cases for editability.

source: Craw, Wiratunga, Rowe (2006) Learning adaptation knowledge to improve case-based reasoning
finding: Search snippet only: adaptation learned as an extra step after nearest-neighbour retrieval, tested on tablet formulation.
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Not opened. Unverified.
agent_relevance: Background for the knowledge-acquisition bottleneck (Hanney and Keane 1996/97, cited in the CAST paper).

source: Guo et al. (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science by Empowering Large Language Models with Case-Based Reasoning
finding: Retrieve one past solved task and have the LLM adapt its code to the new task. Adapting one case beats zero-shot and random-case prompting.
numbers: 18 deployment tasks, one-pass (bug-free code) rate: DS-Agent with GPT-4 about 99-100%, GPT-3.5 85%; best baseline 56% (GPT-3.5) and 60% (GPT-4). Mixtral-8x7b: 6% to 31%. Cost per run $0.0045 (GPT-3.5) and $0.135 (GPT-4) in the low-resource mode.
limits: Authors' own benchmark; case bank built from Kaggle human insights; 5 trials. Self-reported.
agent_relevance: Direct LLM test of the adapt-one-case step (O7). Large gain from one well-chosen case.

source: Guo et al. (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science by Empowering Large Language Models with Case-Based Reasoning
finding: More retrieved cases in context made results worse, not better. The adapter step works on a single example.
numbers: Case-number sweep (Fig. 6b): zero cases is worst; performance falls rapidly as the number of example cases rises above one. Exact values only in a figure.
quote: the presence of more than one example case in the context introduces interference information
limits: Figure-only evidence; one task family.
agent_relevance: Offer one case to edit, not a pile. Many cases cause interference (links to the Interference subfield).

source: Guo et al. (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science by Empowering Large Language Models with Case-Based Reasoning
finding: Re-ranking retrieved cases by execution feedback (revise step) helps; removing it makes the agent plain RAG and it gets worse.
numbers: Development stage, 12 tasks, average best rank (GPT-4): full 2.08, without ReviseRank 2.58. Success rate 100% over 12 tasks for GPT-4.
limits: Rank differences are modest; 5 trials; no significance test reported.
agent_relevance: Feedback from running the edited result should steer which case to use next.

source: Guo et al. (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science by Empowering Large Language Models with Case-Based Reasoning
finding: Adapting a worked, executable case (homogeneous) beat injecting the same lessons as text insights (heterogeneous).
numbers: Fig. 6a: DS-Agent using past solution cases outperformed the text-insight variant on nearly all deployment tasks (no exact numbers in the text).
limits: Figure-only; authors' comparison.
agent_relevance: Store solved examples with their solution, not only a lesson sentence, when the next job is an edit.

source: Guo et al. (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science by Empowering Large Language Models with Case-Based Reasoning
finding: The paper itself flags an echo-chamber risk: reusing LLM-generated cases can amplify model bias.
numbers: Appendix statement, not measured.
limits: No experiment.
agent_relevance: Guard retention: keep only verified successes.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) TextBFGS: A Case-Based Reasoning Approach to Code Optimization via Error-Operator Retrieval
finding: Store the edit operator (what change fixed which error) rather than the whole old solution. Retrieve by error type, then apply the operator.
numbers: Hard subsets: HumanEval-Hard 45 tasks, MBPP-Hard 117 tasks (Qwen3-235B failed pass@1). Case bases: 39 trajectories (HumanEval), 245 (MBPP), k=3. MBPP-Hard Plus pass rate: TextGrad 48.72%, Momentum 58.12%, with case base up to 78.63%. HumanEval-Hard Plus: Momentum 86.67% to 93.33%.
limits: Preprint. Test sets chosen as failures of one model; small N (45). Case base bootstrapped from the same system's successes.
agent_relevance: Strong support for storing edit operators as cases (S9 record), with a small-N caveat.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) TextBFGS: A Case-Based Reasoning Approach to Code Optimization via Error-Operator Retrieval
finding: Error-based retrieval transfers across domains; problem-text retrieval does not. In the same domain, problem similarity is slightly better.
numbers: Cross-domain MBPP with HumanEval case base, Plus pass: problem-based (REMO) 58.12% vs error-based 74.36% (+16.24 points); baseline 48.72%. In-domain HumanEval: 97.56% (REMO) vs 96.34% (error-based).
limits: Differences of 1-2 points on 45 tasks are within noise (about 1 task). Only the cross-domain gap is large.
agent_relevance: Index edits by failure shape, not task wording, when problems differ in surface.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) TextBFGS: A Case-Based Reasoning Approach to Code Optimization via Error-Operator Retrieval
finding: Cases cut cost as well as errors: fewer iterations and fewer tokens than stateless iterative refinement.
numbers: Iterations down to 13.6; total tokens 21.6k, a 50.6% saving versus Momentum (43.7k). One-pass variant 25.2k vs TextGrad 30.9k (-18.4%) at equal 82.22% pass rate.
limits: Single backbone model; token figures from authors.
agent_relevance: Retrieved edit operators can substitute for extra self-critique loops.

source: Pang et al. (2026) CAST: Case-Based Calibration of Adaptive Reasoning and Execution for LLM Tool Use
finding: Past trajectories used as cases to set reasoning budget and catch structural failures, trained in with RL. Here cases act as adaptation knowledge for the model, not as text edited at run time.
numbers: BFCLv2 overall 88.43% (Qwen2.5-7B), +5.85 over SFT and +4.76 over GRPO; Llama-3.2-8B 78.48/78.73 to 80.43; Qwen2.5-Coder-7B Live 74.92/75.07 to 82.43. Average reasoning length cut 26%.
limits: Requires RL training, so not usable as a pure scaffold. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Shows 'adaptation' can mean calibrating effort by past difficulty. Gains larger on harder items, small on easy.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Case bank of (task, plan, success) triplets read by a planner LLM, which adapts them implicitly. Memory gives additive gains over planning alone.
numbers: Ablation: CBR adds HLE +4.5 F1/+7.0 PM, SimpleQA +3.7/+5.3, DeepResearcher +6.7/+8.2 over planning without CBR. GAIA validation 87.88%, test 79.40%. Learning curve DeepResearcher over 5 iterations: no CBR 78.65 to 84.47; non-parametric CBR 79.84 to 84.85; parametric 80.46 to 85.44.
limits: Gap between CBR and no-CBR shrinks to about 0.4 points by iteration 5. Authors note data contamination in DeepResearcher.
agent_relevance: Gains from stored cases are real but small and shrink as the base agent learns the task. Keep expectations modest.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Number of retrieved cases has a small optimum; more cases do not help.
numbers: Table 3, DeepResearcher average F1: K=0 59.9; K=1 63.6; K=2 63.7; K=4 64.5 (peak); K=8 64.1; K=16 63.9; K=32 63.9.
limits: One benchmark family; differences past K=1 are under 1 point.
agent_relevance: Offering 1-4 cases is enough. Matches the DS-Agent finding that extra cases add nothing or hurt.

source: Wang, Mao, Fried, Neubig (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Induce reusable workflows from past runs (abstracted, variables replaced) and supply them to guide new runs.
numbers: WebArena overall success +12.0 points absolute, +51.1% relative over BrowserGym baseline; 2.0 fewer steps per task. Mind2Web +24.6% relative. Online AWM beats baselines by margins that grow with domain gap (8.9 to 14.0 points).
quote: workflows induced offline and online are not fully compatible with each other
limits: Offline plus online workflows combined scored between the two, not above: offline workflows hurt online ones. Workflows induced from wrong trajectories degrade results.
agent_relevance: Abstracted procedures generalise across domains better than raw cases. Do not stack memory sources blindly.

source: Wang, Mao, Fried, Neubig (2024) Agent Workflow Memory (Mind2Web table 4)
finding: Gains from stored workflows are small in strict end-task success on hard generalisation splits.
numbers: Mind2Web cross-task/website/domain task SR with GPT-4: MindAct 2.0/2.0/1.0; AWM-offline 4.8/2.3/0.7; AWM-online 4.0/1.6/1.7. Step success rose more (36.2 to 45.1 cross-task).
limits: Whole-task success stays under 5% in all arms; cross-domain offline SR (0.7) is below baseline (1.0).
agent_relevance: Step-level gains do not guarantee task-level wins. Measure end success.

source: Olausson, Inala, Wang, Gao, Solar-Lezama (2024) Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?
finding: Editing a failed program (self-repair) often does not beat drawing more fresh samples at equal compute.
numbers: HumanEval and APPS with Code Llama, GPT-3.5, GPT-4. Gains modest, vary by subset, sometimes none. More initial samples helped consistently; more repairs per program gave marginal or negative returns.
quote: performance gains are often modest, vary a lot between subsets of the data, and are sometimes not present at all
limits: Programming puzzles only; one feedback-repair round was best.
agent_relevance: Editing is not always cheaper than resampling. Budget check needed before choosing O7 over regenerate.

source: Olausson et al. (2024) Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?
finding: Quality of the diagnosis step is the bottleneck of repair. Better feedback unlocks the gains.
numbers: Human feedback raised GPT-4 repair success 1.58x over GPT-4's own feedback (16 participants, 40 failing programs, 2 feedbacks each). GPT-4 feedback inaccurate 32/80 vs human 7/80; GPT-4 never expressed uncertainty (0/80) vs humans 7/80. A stronger feedback model also lifted Code Llama and GPT-3.5 above their baselines on APPS.
limits: Small human study.
agent_relevance: For edits, diagnose the difference between old and new problem first, with an outside check. A model's own feedback is weak.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Reported self-correction gains came from using the correct answer to decide when to stop. Without it, accuracy drops.
numbers: GPT-3.5 with oracle: GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3, CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 89.7. Intrinsic (no oracle): GSM8K 75.9 to 74.7, CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 41.8. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after two rounds, HotpotQA 49.0 to 43.0.
quote: LLMs struggle to self-correct their reasoning in this setting
limits: Reasoning tasks only; later work finds gains with trained or tool-based critics.
agent_relevance: Never let the model grade its own edit without an external check. Revise only when a verifier fails.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: When self-correction changes an answer it more often breaks a correct one than fixes a wrong one.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5: 74.7% of answers unchanged after two rounds; among changed ones, correct-to-incorrect exceeded incorrect-to-correct. CommonSenseQA: many correct-to-incorrect flips because wrong options look relevant.
limits: Percent from paper text; the flip table is in a figure.
agent_relevance: A revise step needs a keep-if-better rule.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners
finding: Self-generated relevant exemplars (the model recalls similar problems, then solves) can match or beat retrieved ones when the model is strong enough.
numbers: GSM8K accuracy, text-davinci-003: 0-shot CoT 50%, 5-shot fixed 54%, 5-shot retrieved 57%, self-generated 61%. Weaker models: text-davinci-002 47% retrieved vs 48% self; text-davinci-001 11% vs 9%; curie 3% vs 2%.
limits: Self-generation fails for weak models. Retrieval is more reliable when labelled data exists. Old OpenAI models.
agent_relevance: If our memory is empty, the model can recall its own analogous cases; with a real memory, retrieved cases are safer for small models.

source: Lewis and Mitchell (2024) Using Counterfactual Tasks to Evaluate the Generality of Analogical Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Failed generalisation of an earlier claim: GPT models that matched humans on letter-string analogies drop sharply when the alphabet is permuted or replaced by symbols.
numbers: Humans: 136 participants, accuracy 0.753 (1,876 samples). GPT samples 6,840 each: GPT-3 0.488, GPT-3.5 0.350, GPT-4 0.452. Human accuracy stayed flat across permuted alphabets. Comprehension checks showed models understood the new ordering.
limits: Letter-string toy domain; 2023 models. Counterfactual alphabets are unusual by design.
agent_relevance: Mapping a known solution onto a changed surface is a weak point: the edit may copy surface form. Test our adapter on altered versions of stored cases.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Case-Based or Rule-Based: How Do Transformers Do the Math?
finding: Fine-tuned transformers solve unseen arithmetic by leaning on neighbouring training cases (case-based) and fail in held-out regions. Explicit rule following fixes it.
numbers: Leave-Square-Out test: accuracy collapses inside held-out squares, worse as the square grows (side 10 to 40). Rule-Following Fine-Tuning: training on 1-5 digit addition generalises to 12 digits with over 95% accuracy, 40+ points above scratchpad.
limits: Fine-tuned small models (GPT-2, Llama-2-7B, GPT-3.5 via API); not scaffolds.
agent_relevance: Case similarity alone does not extend past the edge of stored cases. An explicit rule or operator is needed for the edit.

source: Review of Case-Based Reasoning for LLM Agents (2025)
finding: Conceptual review: proposes transformational, compositional and generative adaptation operators for LLM agents. Contains no new measurement of adaptation.
numbers: No experiments on adaptation; comparison table uses qualitative ratings (adaptation capacity 'moderate').
limits: Position paper; treat as vocabulary, not evidence.
agent_relevance: Three edit types to name in O7: substitute/delete/insert, merge parts of several cases, regenerate guided by a case.

source: DomAgent (2026) Knowledge graphs and case-based reasoning for domain-specific code generation
finding: Retrieved cases plus an LLM that edits them lift small models a lot in a narrow domain; choosing cases by knowledge-graph coverage beats random choice.
numbers: Truck CAN signal code, pass@1: vanilla Qwen2.5-7B 39.62, GPT-4o 71.22; +KG adds 31.27 / 16.58 points; +CBR adds a further 44.95 / 19.88 points; full system 96.64 (Qwen) and 98.04 (GPT-4o). KG-selected 30% of cases roughly equals random 80%.
limits: Narrow, templated industrial domain with internal docs; gains likely inflated. Dataset not public.
agent_relevance: Case selection for coverage lets a small case base work. Gains largest where the domain is narrow and repetitive.
